topic_ko: 미래 대비형 도시 — 같은 공간, 변화하는 용도
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 31번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다. order/insert/irrelevant/writing 은 구조상 예외.

passage: One feature of a city street or square that is easy to overlook is how well it resists becoming obsolete over time.
The ancient medieval squares of cities such as Marrakesh and Siena are still places where goods are sold every single day.
What is sold there has changed enormously across the past five hundred years, yet the squares themselves carry on unchanged.
A city square, like a shopping street, is therefore a remarkably durable technology, even in an age dominated by online shopping.
The very same shop that once sold buggy whips and typewriters might today repair cracked phones and serve bubble tea.
In other words, one fixed set of physical structures quietly supports a stream of constantly evolving uses.
Jane Jacobs, the great prophet of the city economy, made much of this point in her writings.
She correctly foresaw that the city would persist, contradicting those who claimed the Internet would bring about its death.
choices: how a city's physical spaces endure by supporting ever-changing uses
why online shopping is gradually replacing traditional city streets
how medieval squares were originally designed and constructed
why famous urban thinkers often disagree about a city's future
how modern stores decide which products will sell most quickly
theme.explanation_ko: 도시의 거리나 광장은 같은 물리적 구조가 시대마다 바뀌는 용도를 떠받치며 사라지지 않는다는 내용. '도시 공간이 변화하는 용도를 지탱하며 지속된다'가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ②온라인 쇼핑의 대체, ③광장의 건축·설계, ④학자들의 의견 차이, ⑤상점의 상품 선택은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: When we think about cities, we should not dismiss old streets and squares as relics waiting to be replaced.
The medieval squares of Marrakesh and Siena still host daily trade, even though the goods on offer have changed completely.
A single storefront that once sold typewriters may now repair phones and sell bubble tea, all within the same walls.
This shows that durable physical infrastructure can keep serving a society whose needs never stop shifting.
Jane Jacobs, who studied the city economy deeply, emphasized exactly this adaptive strength.
She rightly predicted the survival of the city, unlike those who expected the Internet to make it disappear.
We should therefore value and preserve such flexible urban spaces rather than treating them as outdated.
Their worth lies precisely in their capacity to absorb change without being torn down.
choices: 도시의 오래된 거리와 광장은 변화를 수용하는 가치 있는 공간으로 보존해야 한다.
온라인 쇼핑 시대에는 전통적 상점가를 점차 없애 나가야 한다.
도시 계획은 유명 학자의 예측에 전적으로 의존해서는 안 된다.
오래된 건물은 안전을 위해 가능한 한 빨리 재건축해야 한다.
상인들은 시대에 맞춰 판매 품목을 자주 바꾸어야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 같은 물리적 공간이 변화하는 용도를 지탱하므로 그러한 유연한 도시 공간을 낡은 것으로 취급하지 말고 보존·가치화해야 한다는 주장. ①이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ②③④⑤는 본문의 핵심 주장과 무관하거나 지엽적이다.

passage: A city street or square has a quietly valuable quality: it rarely becomes useless even as the world around it changes.
Squares in Marrakesh and Siena have sold goods every day for centuries, though the goods themselves are now entirely different.
The same store that once offered buggy whips and typewriters may today repair phones and serve bubble tea.
One unchanging structure thus keeps supporting a long succession of evolving uses.
Jane Jacobs called attention to this very feature when she wrote about the life of cities.
She predicted, correctly, that the city would endure rather than vanish in the Internet age.
The strength of urban architecture lies in its ability to host change without being rebuilt.
Old spaces survive precisely because they bend to new purposes.
choices: 도시의 거리와 광장은 같은 구조로 변화하는 용도를 떠받치며 지속된다.
인터넷의 등장은 결국 전통적 도시를 사라지게 만들 것이다.
중세 광장은 오늘날의 상업 공간보다 훨씬 효율적이었다.
도시 경제를 이해하려면 반드시 건축사를 먼저 배워야 한다.
상점은 살아남기 위해 끊임없이 새로운 상품을 들여와야 한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 변하지 않는 물리적 구조가 끊임없이 바뀌는 용도를 지탱하여 도시가 지속된다는 것이 요지. ①이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ②도시 소멸, ③광장의 효율 비교, ④건축사 학습, ⑤상품 교체는 요지가 아니다.

passage: Among a city's least appreciated strengths is the way its streets and squares refuse to go out of date.
The medieval squares of Marrakesh and Siena still bustle with daily commerce after five hundred years.
The merchandise has changed completely, but the squares keep doing the same fundamental job.
A storefront that once sold typewriters may now repair phones and pour bubble tea.
The infrastructure stays fixed while the uses it shelters keep evolving.
Jane Jacobs, the great prophet of the city economy, built much of her thinking on this insight.
She foresaw the city's survival, even as others announced its death at the hands of the Internet.
Cities last, it turns out, because their bones can hold many different lives.
choices: Old Spaces, New Uses: Why Cities Never Go Obsolete
The Internet and the Coming Death of the City
How Medieval Squares Were Built to Last
Bubble Tea: The Surprising Future of Retail
Jane Jacobs and the Decline of Modern Economics
title.explanation_ko: 같은 공간이 새로운 용도를 떠받치며 사라지지 않는다는 핵심을 압축한 ①이 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ②도시 소멸, ③광장 건축, ④버블티 자체, ⑤경제학 쇠퇴는 초점이 아니다.

passage: It is easy to forget how stubbornly a city street or square resists becoming obsolete.
The squares of Marrakesh and Siena have sold goods daily for half a millennium, though the goods have changed beyond recognition.
A shop that once sold typewriters may now repair phones and serve bubble tea.
In every case, the same infrastructure supports evolving uses.
Jane Jacobs grasped this when she wrote about how a city economy survives.
Unlike those who expected the Internet to kill the city, she knew its bones could hold many different lives.
The walls stay put while the purpose poured into them is endlessly refilled.
The building never asks what era it is in; it simply keeps making room.
implication.underlined: its bones could hold many different lives
choices: the city's old buildings are physically too strong to ever collapse
one fixed structure can keep serving many changing purposes over time
people living in cities tend to move from one home to another
urban architecture must be rebuilt for each new generation
city economies depend mainly on the predictions of experts
implication.explanation_ko: '그 뼈대가 여러 다른 삶을 담을 수 있다'는 비유는 하나의 고정된 구조가 시대마다 바뀌는 여러 용도를 계속 수용한다는 뜻이다. ②가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①물리적 견고함, ③거주 이동, ④세대마다 재건축, ⑤전문가 예측 의존은 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: One feature of a city street that is easy to overlook is how well it resists becoming obsolete.

grammar.explanation_ko: ⑤ those who 뒤에는 정동사가 와야 하는 관계절이므로 분사 predicting이 아니라 과거형 정동사 predicted가 옳다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①동명사 becoming(resist의 목적어), ②관계부사 where(places 수식), ③주격 관계절 that once sold, ④단수 주어 set에 호응하는 supports는 모두 옳다.

passage: One feature of a city street that is easy to overlook is how well it resists becoming obsolete.

vocab.explanation_ko: ③ 도시 광장은 수백 년간 사라지지 않는 '내구성 있는(durable)' 기술이라는 문맥이므로, '일시적인(temporary)'은 정반대 의미라 부적절하다. durable로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①obsolete(구식이 됨에 저항), ②unchanged(변치 않음), ④evolving(진화하는 용도), ⑤persistence(지속)는 문맥에 적절하다.

blank.explanation_ko: 타자기 가게가 휴대폰 수리·버블티 가게로 바뀐 예시처럼, 같은 구조가 끊임없이 바뀌는 용도(evolving uses)를 떠받친다. ②가 정답.

order.given: One easily overlooked feature of a city street or square is its "future-proof" nature, its ability to keep serving us as the world changes around it.

blocks.A: For example, the very same storefront that once sold buggy whips and typewriters might now repair cracked phones and serve bubble tea.
blocks.B: The ancient medieval squares of Marrakesh and Siena prove the point, for they are still places where goods are sold every day, even though the goods have changed across five centuries.
blocks.C: In short, the same infrastructure supports evolving uses, which is why Jane Jacobs correctly predicted the persistence of the city against those who foresaw its death.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글의 '미래 대비형'을 (B)가 광장 사례로 입증, (A)가 'For example'로 한 가게의 용도 변화를 구체화, (C)가 'In short'로 요약·Jacobs로 마무리. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 In short는 앞선 사례들을 요약하므로 첫 순서가 될 수 없고, (A)의 For example은 일반 진술(B) 뒤라야 한다.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 한 가게의 용도 변화를 보여 주는 구체적 'For example'이며, '광장·상점가가 미래 대비형 기술'이라는 일반 진술(③) 뒤이자 '같은 구조가 변화하는 용도를 지탱한다'는 일반화(④ 문장) 앞에 와야 한다. ④가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 예시가 없으면 'The same infrastructure supports evolving uses'라는 일반화의 근거가 사라진다.

summary.summary_template: Although the goods and activities inside city spaces constantly __(A)__, the spaces themselves endure because one fixed structure can __(B)__ ever-new uses.
summary.explanation_ko: 도시 공간 안의 활동은 끊임없이 (A)change(변하)지만, 고정된 구조가 새로운 용도를 (B)accommodate(수용)하기에 공간은 지속된다. ③.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 change, (B)는 accommodate여야 한다. reject/limit 등은 반대 의미이다.
